title: Apple Proposes 15% Commission on Purchases Made Outside the App Store
summary: Apple has submitted a proposal to the U.S. District Court of Northern California outlining its planned commission structure for purchases made via external links within iOS apps. The proposal includes a 15% commission for standard apps, with reduced rates for small businesses (5%), developers in special programs (10%), and subscription renewals (10%). This follows a legal battle with Epic Games and a Supreme Court decision rejecting Apple's attempt to delay the proceedings.
key_points: Apple proposes a 15% commission on purchases made outside the App Store via external links in iOS apps.
Reduced commissions for small businesses (5%) and developers in special programs (10%).
Subscription renewals would incur a 10% commission.
The proposal follows a legal dispute with Epic Games over App Store policies.
Apple argued for delays, but the Supreme Court rejected its bid to pause lower court proceedings.
Apple justifies the fees as necessary to recoup investments in the App Store ecosystem.
Comparison made to Google Play's link-out fees (20% for standard apps, 15% for special programs, 10% for subscriptions).
